title: runbook-dryrun-orchestrator: staged simulation and approval workflow for admin tasks
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: On-call engineers and SREs need a low-risk way to validate runbooks-as-tasks against real state without impacting production. Currently engineers must choose between ad-hoc manual dry-runs or limited unit tests; both miss systemic interactions (caches, KV state, routing).

Goal: Build a Runbook Dry-Run Orchestrator (RDO) that executes runbooks-as-tasks in configurable staged modes (read-only simulation, time-delayed emulate, and staged mutation with rollback gates) and integrates an approval workflow to promote a dry-run to a production rollout. RDO should plug into existing runbook task runner, provide recorded traces for post-mortem, and surface safety checks in the Console.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- Provide three modes: Observe (read-only simulation), Emulate (simulate mutations using shadow subsystems and synthetic KV), and StagedApply (apply to subset with automatic rollback on SLO violations).
- Integrates with runbook DSL and the existing runbook task graph executor with <= 2% added latency for normal runs.
- Exposes approval gates (manual and automated) and an audit trail visible in Console and logs.
- Dry-run traces must be recordable to the existing telemetry pipeline and linkable from incident timelines.

Technical approach summary:
- Add an RDO orchestration layer that can stub or shadow downstream effects: e.g., route writes to sandboxed KV namespace, fork outbound API calls to a mock harness, and capture pre/post state diffs.
- Implement an emulation harness that can replay historical traffic samples for timing-sensitive steps.
- Hook into the existing runbook task scheduler with a 'simulation mode' flag. Use feature flags to enable incremental rollout.
- Build lightweight approval microservice integrated with Console routes and Slack notifications for manual gates.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Track dry-run counts, simulation failures, mismatches between dry-run and production run outputs, average time to approval, and number of rollbacks triggered.
- Create Dashboard card in Console under 'Ops Automation' with drilldowns to traces.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Emulation may miss side-effects of external systems. Mitigation: Start with safe, local subsystems (KV, cache) and expand to networked APIs via request recording/playback.
- Risk: Complexity adds latency to runbook execution. Mitigation: Ensure simulation path is isolated and opt-in; production paths default to fast path.

Rollout plan:
1) POC internal-only with Observe mode and a handful of core runbooks (2 weeks).
2) Emulate mode with sandboxed KV and API mocks for critical flows (3 weeks).
3) StagedApply with approval and rollback gates for non-production seeds (4 weeks).
4) Beta with selected customers (Dedicated) and Console UI in ops-2025.03 release.

Notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration, APIs, and safety gates. Separate follow-ups will cover Console UI polish, extended mock library, and RBAC integration.
